nodes.title: Budget Stabilisation Compact
nodes.description: Reinforce the stabilisation programme through firmer collection and restrained social commitments. The state improves its finances and borrowing position, while accepting disillusion among supporters who expected a broader expansion of provision.
nodes.history: The 1983 turn to rigueur placed external and monetary stability ahead of the earlier expansionary pace; the compact is a policy abstraction. Numerical values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: Coalition Government
nodes.description: Accept the compromises needed to keep a broad left government in office. Administrative cooperation and a more credible public settlement support revenue collection, while coalition negotiation limits the party’s freedom of action and sustains its social promises.
nodes.history: The PCF joined the 1972 Common Programme and entered the Mauroy government in 1981; the specific governing sequence is alternate history. Numerical values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: Independent Communist Initiative
nodes.description: Keep communist priorities visible through a distinct programme of industrial direction and organised labour. Independent initiative can sharpen economic coordination, but it makes coalition maintenance harder and narrows office-sector growth.
nodes.history: The PCF retained an independent identity inside the Union of the Left and government; its disagreements with the PS later strained the alliance. Numerical values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: A Unified Public Industry Plan
nodes.description: Guarantee large orders and direct inputs through a single public plan. Sustained series benefit from central allocation, but energy use and slower adaptation are real burdens.
nodes.history: PCF-led public ownership and planning are policy precedents; the governing path and numerical values are alternate-history balance proposals.

nodes.title: Municipal Industrial Compacts
nodes.description: Give public firms and municipalities room to renew workshops and local services together. Repair and civilian output improve while national arms orders lose priority.
nodes.history: The PCF’s municipal base and common-programme commitments provide precedents for local bargaining; this national arrangement is alternate history. Numerical values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: Planned Specialisation
nodes.description: Use stable production targets to concentrate established factories on selected industrial priorities. The plan raises their attainable output, while fixed targets make adaptation to changing demand more difficult.
nodes.history: A centralised industrial plan is consistent with the old guard’s orthodox programme; the focus is an alternate governing extension. Numerical values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: Production Campaigns
nodes.description: Mobilise party and workplace organisations around immediate production targets. Intensive mobilisation can improve factory efficiency, but repeated campaigns disrupt public confidence and routine economic planning.
nodes.history: Workplace mobilisation is consistent with the old guard’s emphasis on party direction; the focus is an alternate governing extension. Numerical values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: Worker Cooperatives
nodes.description: Help workers preserve productive capacity by converting threatened enterprises into worker-run cooperatives. Enterprise participation can improve adaptation, while lower output ceilings and public support obligations limit the immediate return.
nodes.history: Lip’s 1973 worker self-management and PSU advocacy of autogestion are precedents; nationwide conversion is alternate history. Numerical values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: Regional Skills
nodes.description: Develop regional technical institutes and public-works skills alongside workplace autonomy. Better construction planning and productive adaptation require a continuing education commitment.
nodes.history: The PSU’s autogestionnaire programme and local experiments provide precedents; the national compact is alternate history. Numerical values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: Indexed Wage Settlement
nodes.description: Extend sectoral wage agreements and a dependable wage floor as the price of industrial peace. More predictable labour relations support productive adaptation, while a broader social settlement raises recurring public obligations.
nodes.history: Inspired by Chaban-Delmas’s Nouvelle Société and the 1970 SMIC reform; a national council system is a roleplay proposal.

nodes.title: Skills and Participation
nodes.description: Put vocational skills and employee participation ahead of further wage commitments. Joint training and modernisation improve productive capability, while the education programme requires sustained public financing.
nodes.history: A counterfactual extension of Chaban’s participation agenda; the 1970 SMIC reform is a precedent for linking wages to the fruits of growth.

nodes.title: Investment Mandate
nodes.description: Give strategic firms a defined modernisation mandate and judge support by their delivery of national industrial priorities. Coordination strengthens industrial investment, while adding a continuing administrative burden.
nodes.history: State coordination and national champions are established Gaullist policy themes; this performance-linked mandate is a roleplay proposal.

nodes.title: Export Modernisation
nodes.description: Prepare industrial groups to compete through process renewal and technical skills. Publicly supported training improves their productive potential, while placing a continuing obligation on education expenditure.
nodes.history: A counterfactual continuation of Gaullist industrial direction, consistent with post-war planning and the later policy of national champions.

nodes.title: Fiscal Accountability
nodes.description: Give the audit authorities and tax administration the resources to improve collection and publish credible public accounts. A stronger revenue base requires an administration capable of enforcing the rules.
nodes.history: The Barre government’s post-1976 stabilisation is the precedent; an independent review institution is a roleplay design.

nodes.title: Technical Skills
nodes.description: Protect technical education and workplace training through the adjustment programme, so fiscal credibility does not hollow out future industrial capacity. Research advances faster, with a higher education bill.
nodes.history: A plausible liberal-modernising response to the post-1973 adjustment; this compact is a counterfactual policy instrument.

nodes.title: Regional Credit
nodes.description: Use continuing investment incentives to sustain industrial renewal in the regions. New projects become easier to undertake, while the incentives reduce the corporate tax receipts available to the state.
nodes.history: Giscard’s 1974 public statements support activity and state assistance for industrial redeployment; this credit scheme is a roleplay proposal.

nodes.title: Employment Transition
nodes.description: Protect workers and industrial communities while enterprises restructure. Sustained transition assistance makes adjustment more acceptable, at the cost of a continuing social commitment.
nodes.history: The employment and adjustment challenge is documented in Giscard’s 1974 economic statements; the transition fund is a counterfactual instrument.

nodes.title: Strategic Supply Allocation
nodes.description: Reserve extraction, stocks and contracts for strategically important production. The arrangement improves resilience under sanctions but ties civilian firms to administrative allocation.
nodes.history: A counterfactual orthodox-Gaullist extension of national economic direction; the Fifth Republic’s planning institutions provide context, not proof of this exact policy.

nodes.title: Independent Supplier Compacts
nodes.description: Support a wider supplier base with investment access and procurement credit. More adaptable firms require continuing tax concessions rather than compulsory allocations.
nodes.history: A counterfactual alternative within the orthodox Gaullist national-independence programme, balancing public direction with private execution.

nodes.title: Business Tax Relief
nodes.description: Answer the small-trader revolt with business investment relief. Commercial development becomes more attractive, while the state accepts a lower corporate tax yield; the relief is represented across MD’s business tax base.
nodes.history: The late-1960s and early-1970s Nicoud-led CID mobilised against taxation and administrative burdens; this governing programme is alternate history.

nodes.title: Local Licences
nodes.description: Devolve routine commercial licensing and reduce the weight of central administration. Independent enterprise gains room to develop, while Paris gives up part of its direct political initiative.
nodes.history: Administrative simplification reflects CID’s protest against state burdens; a national licensing compact is a roleplay proposal.

nodes.title: Municipal Services
nodes.description: Turn an electoral strategy into dependable municipal government and local services. A broader public settlement supports commercial activity, while social provision carries a recurring fiscal cost.
nodes.history: FN municipal activity and its later electoral breakthrough are precedents; this governing compact is alternate history.

nodes.title: Executive Enforcement
nodes.description: Extend the confrontational programme through a more coordinated internal-security administration. Political initiative grows, at the price of further policing expense and a less stable settlement.
nodes.history: The FN’s later confrontational electoral strategy is historical context; an executive security network under a governing FN is alternate history.

nodes.title: Executive Coordination
nodes.description: A presidential majority must turn its mandate into coordinated administration. Give the government a stronger capacity to carry decisions across ministries, accepting a narrower margin for deliberation.
nodes.history: Counterfactual institutional development from the Fifth Republic's strengthened presidency; balance values are design proposals.

nodes.title: Constitutional Review
nodes.description: A parliamentary safeguard matters only if an opposition able to assemble a substantial minority can use it. Open constitutional review to sixty deputies or senators, accepting a slower route from legislation to promulgation.
nodes.history: The constitutional revision of 29 October 1974 first allowed sixty deputies or sixty senators to refer a law to the Constitutional Council; an earlier adoption is an alternate-history choice.

nodes.title: Mutual Insurance
nodes.description: Transfer part of state-financed care to member-funded mutual coverage and grant household tax relief for contributions. The proposal lowers public health expenditure while reducing population-tax receipts. It extends the historical complementary role of mutual societies rather than claiming they replaced compulsory Social Security.
nodes.history: The 1898 Mutuality Charter recognised French mutual societies' solidarist identity; after 1945, mutuality operated as complementary protection alongside compulsory Social Security. A larger role under this government is a policy choice.

nodes.title: Public Health Guarantee
nodes.description: A social market requires common standards that do not depend on a household's access to a mutual society. Expand the public health commitment, accepting a substantially greater continuing claim on health expenditure.
nodes.history: France's 1945 Social Security settlement established compulsory public protection; the exact expansion proposed here is an alternate policy. The 1945–1967 mutualist debate documents the competing roles of statutory and complementary insurance.

nodes.title: Public Engineering Institutes
nodes.description: Fund public laboratories and engineering schools with a stable research mandate. The technical workforce benefits, while military construction competes with a stronger civilian claim on investment.
nodes.history: Servan-Schreiber's 1969–1970 Radical renewal addressed the technological society; the 1971 law made continuing vocational education a national obligation shared by the state, local authorities, education, unions and firms. This contract programme is a plausible extension.

nodes.title: Small-Firm Innovation Guarantees
nodes.description: Use credit guarantees to carry independent firms through development and production. A dispersed innovation network requires tax concessions and accepts uneven results.
nodes.history: Servan-Schreiber's Radical manifesto argued for renewing technological enterprise while preventing economic power from ruling without restraint. A targeted guarantee is a balance proposal inspired by that programme, not a recorded 1970 law.

nodes.title: Industrial Conversion
nodes.description: Renew industrial processes and workforce skills as part of an ecological reform programme. Industrial modernisation improves productive capability, while standards slow new industrial construction and training requires public financing. The research bonus supports industry; it does not create an environmental technology category.
nodes.history: France established a national environment ministry in 1971 and adopted a waste-disposal law in 1975. Industrial conversion is a plausible programme inspired by this period's emerging environmental politics; an ecology-led government from 1970 is alternate history.

nodes.title: Landscape and Local Works
nodes.description: Combine conservation review with municipal infrastructure and local services around protected landscapes. Local works and a more settled development policy offer practical gains, while review constrains industrial expansion and requires administration. These effects do not directly simulate biodiversity.
nodes.history: The 1976 Nature Protection Act recognised natural spaces, landscapes, species, biological balances and natural resources as matters of general interest. Enacting a stronger conservation code is a policy choice grounded in that precedent.

nodes.title: Housing Contracts
nodes.description: Give the redistributive programme a practical outlet in housing and public construction. Strengthen construction planning and the capacity to carry projects through, accepting a sustained social commitment.
nodes.history: Public housing and social investment are historical policy precedents; this allocation and its values are roleplay proposals.

nodes.title: Mechanised Conscription
nodes.description: Maintain an army of trained conscripts and mechanised formations for a major European emergency. Reinforcement and doctrine gain priority, with a larger supply requirement.
nodes.history: Alternate extension of the 1966 withdrawal from NATO's integrated command. France retained Alliance membership and arrangements for possible joint operations in Germany; the 1970 debate linked deterrence, territorial defence, and capacity to intervene in Europe.

nodes.title: A Mobile Intervention Cadre
nodes.description: Preserve a specialist intervention cadre, supported by regular air-wing exercises and trained recovery services. The force gains practice and endurance without an automatic deployment or foreign commitment, while professional personnel require sustained expenditure.
nodes.history: Conscription, reserve preparation, and territorial defence were central in the 1970 defence debate; privileging reserves is a policy alternative, not a claim about an enacted reform.

nodes.title: Undersea and Command Continuity
nodes.description: Protect the independent deterrent’s industrial base and naval command skills. Shipyard priority constrains new land-armament investment; it grants no warheads or strategic authority.
nodes.history: France maintained a national nuclear command while treating territorial defence and intervention capacity as linked duties. The 1970 defence debate supports this conventional readiness programme; no new nuclear capability is granted.

nodes.title: Conventional Freedom of Action
nodes.description: Give France the trained conventional forces and sustainment capacity needed below the nuclear threshold. Greater freedom to act brings an enduring personnel commitment.
nodes.history: The 1970 programme debate covered national service, reserve preparation, operational unity among services, and equipment costs. This is a counterfactual training priority.

nodes.title: Professional Sustainment Corps
nodes.description: Pay the maintenance and training specialists needed to keep land and air units serviceable. Fewer supplies and fewer flying accidents reward professional standards, at the expense of a larger army and air-force payroll.
nodes.history: The 1970 national-service debate covered service length, conditions, volunteer numbers, and the balance of conscripts and professionals. A specialist cadre is an alternate modernising programme.

nodes.title: A Technical Citizen Reserve
nodes.description: Preserve a technically trained reserve on a restrained standing-force budget. Reinforcement depth and lower pay costs require longer initial training and dependable civilian employers.
nodes.history: National service and reserve preparation were active subjects in the 1970 debate. Choosing a broad reserve system over professionalisation is a counterfactual programme.

nodes.title: Territorial Engineer Service
nodes.description: Train military engineers and reserve services to keep roads, depots and civil protection working. Useful territorial skills require a regular service and equipment budget.
nodes.history: The 1970 defence debate linked conscription and territorial defence to the national character of the armed forces. This civil-defence emphasis is an alternative programme.

nodes.title: Maritime and Joint-Service Readiness
nodes.description: Train crews and staffs together around escort procedures, navigation and safe operation. Doctrine and accident prevention improve through a continuing naval personnel commitment, rather than a free expansion of the fleet.
nodes.history: Operational unity among the three services appeared in the 1970 defence-programme debate. A permanent joint-service review is a counterfactual institutional response.

nodes.title: Six-Month Service and Regional Reserves
nodes.description: Develop the Common Programme’s shorter service and trained regional reserves as a governing alternative. A lighter standing payroll buys mobilisation depth while specialist preparation takes longer.
nodes.history: French defence policy retained conscription alongside strategic independence through the 1970s and 1980s. The reserve emphasis is an alternate policy choice; values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: A Rapid Action Force
nodes.description: Prioritise a trained rapid-action cadre while retaining civilian authority over deployments. Readiness and sustainment improve, but professional personnel make a lasting claim on the social budget.
nodes.history: France combined conscription with a professional strategic force; this choice shifts emphasis toward cadre quality without removing either institution. Numerical modifiers are design proposals.

nodes.title: Regional Popular Defence
nodes.description: Translate the Common Programme’s trained regional reserves into a defensive military institution. Territorial defence improves while longer preparation limits immediate expeditionary readiness.
nodes.history: The PCF's national-defence tradition and organised labour base provide precedents for a civic reserve emphasis. The national programme is alternate history; France's independent deterrent and conscription remain intact.

nodes.title: Public General Staff and Technical Schools
nodes.description: Fund the staff and technical schools needed to operate a modern public armaments sector. This is a governing extrapolation, with specialist education rather than foreign command at its centre.
nodes.history: A tightly supervised party-state command is a plausible governing alternative for the PCF, rather than a claim that it controlled the armed forces in historical France. Values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: Mass Territorial Establishments
nodes.description: Maintain a large trained territorial reserve with a restrained professional establishment. Depth depends on longer training and a less immediately available force.
nodes.history: Conscription remained central to the French model through the period. This choice strengthens its reserve and territorial-defence emphasis rather than changing the nuclear or alliance settlement.

nodes.title: Central Technical Staff
nodes.description: Concentrate scarce specialists in a central staff and maintenance corps. This counterfactual hard-line programme buys readiness through sustained professional expenditure.
nodes.history: The professional cadre complements rather than replaces conscription in the historical French force structure. Numerical modifiers are balance proposals.

nodes.title: A Civilian-Controlled Technical Force
nodes.description: Retain a small technical force under parliamentary authority, with accountable counter-infiltration and supply services. A professional core costs more than a civic reserve.
nodes.history: The PSU's anti-militarist and democratic traditions support civilian oversight, while retaining France's actual conscript and deterrent framework. The smaller-force emphasis is an alternative programme, not a free army expansion.

nodes.title: Popular Defence and Civil Service
nodes.description: Explore the PSU’s later popular-defence current through reserve engineering and civil service. Civilian resilience and territorial preparation take priority over central arms throughput.
nodes.history: The PSU emerged from anti-war and democratic-socialist currents; citizen defence is a plausible institutional alternative, not a claim that the PSU controlled the historical armed forces. Values are balance proposals.

nodes.title: A Republican Territorial Reserve
nodes.description: Tie reserve service to territorial units and civilian oversight. A prepared home defence gains depth at the cost of slower training cycles for the standing force.
nodes.history: Servan-Schreiber’s 1970 Radical manifesto called for reform rather than rupture. A territorially anchored reserve is a plausible institutional extension, not a recorded Radical defence plan.

nodes.title: Technical Defence Establishments
nodes.description: Maintain a smaller technical establishment through engineering education and applied trials. Better doctrine and sustainment depend on continuing public education expenditure.
nodes.history: The Radical emphasis on technological modernisation informs this alternate professional cadre; no new divisions or equipment are created by the policy.

nodes.title: A Territorial Rescue Service
nodes.description: Build rescue, engineering and emergency logistics around existing civil-protection services. Repair capacity has a continuing personnel cost; it creates neither troops nor an automatic foreign deployment.
nodes.history: The 1970 environment programme and 1971 ministry created cross-ministerial duties but had limited means. This alternative invests in civil protection rather than claiming automatic nuclear disarmament.

nodes.title: A Small Protective Force
nodes.description: Preserve a professional defensive force rather than converting every military workshop to civilian service. Efficient territorial defence requires a larger standing payroll.
nodes.history: The limited professional option is counterfactual. The modifier raises recurring weekly army personnel expense according to the active force; it grants no units or equipment.

nodes.title: A Lean Standing Establishment
nodes.description: Restrain the regular establishment and extend the life of existing equipment. Lower weekly costs leave fewer trained replacements immediately available.
nodes.history: The CID (Comité d’information et de défense), led by Gérard Nicoud, mobilised independent shopkeepers and artisans over social-insurance charges, taxation and large-store competition. This fiscal-lean military choice is alternate history.

nodes.title: Employer-Supported Reservists
nodes.description: Pay independent employers to retain trained reservists and emergency workshops. Mobilisation and repair improve through a tax concession that reduces public revenue.
nodes.history: The CID’s small-shopkeeper base informs the local supplier emphasis; a reserve-industrial compact is counterfactual and not a documented CID platform.

nodes.title: Territorial National Service
nodes.description: Prioritise national service and territorial mobilisation. This is an alternate governing programme: it strengthens home defence but takes longer to train than a specialist standing force.
nodes.history: The 1973 FN programme stressed national defence and a confederal European framework. This conscription route is a counterfactual governing policy; it grants no manpower or equipment.

nodes.title: A Professional Intervention Establishment
nodes.description: Fund a professional force able to act beyond territorial defence. It offers readiness without automatic intervention, alongside a substantial recurring payroll.
nodes.history: The 1973 platform endorsed French defence and proposed European coordination, including a British-French nuclear proposal. This focus models only an expensive conventional cadre; it creates no nuclear or automatic treaty.

nodes.title: National Arsenal Series
nodes.description: The DMA's inherited arsenals and the new inter-service procurement system give the Republic a base for long production runs, but each new programme competes with social and regional investment. This route directs capital toward French-designed armoured vehicles and protected supply contracts. It favours sovereign land power and dependable series over cheaper imports or a wider European division of work.

nodes.description: A steady order book lets French plants preserve skilled teams and carry a vehicle line through successive improvements. The advantage comes from keeping one design in production long enough for workers and suppliers to master it; the cost is less flexibility when requirements change. This continuation puts the army's armoured fleet ahead of short runs across several competing equipment types.

nodes.title: European Airframe Workshare
nodes.description: European aircraft cooperation can spread the cost of advanced design while keeping French engineers inside the programme. This route builds shared airframe standards and a trained technical workforce, drawing on the industrial logic that produced Airbus. Partners gain a voice in workshare and export choices, however, so France trades some unilateral control for a broader base of skills and production.

nodes.title: Shared Components and Tooling
nodes.description: Common components and tooling allow French and partner plants to supply a shared airframe with fewer duplicated processes. The arrangement raises civilian productivity as expertise moves across the industrial network, but it also deepens exposure to outside decisions and supply interruptions. France retains its command authority while accepting that a cooperative aircraft programme cannot be directed from Paris alone.

nodes.title: Protected Naval Arsenals
nodes.description: France's strategic deterrent depends on a national industrial base, trained naval crews and the ability to maintain its submarines at home. This programme gives the naval arsenals priority and protects the continuity of undersea design expertise. Dockyard investment and specialist schools are costly commitments; land factories must wait while the force de frappe remains credible and under French command.

nodes.title: Undersea Design Continuity
nodes.description: The undersea fleet requires engineering knowledge that cannot be assembled only when a refit is due. Continuous design work and naval education preserve the cadres who keep French submarines and their support systems serviceable. The commitment strengthens national command at sea, but its long training horizon and public cost leave fewer resources for immediate conventional procurement.

nodes.title: Sovereign Land Procurement
nodes.description: A sovereign land force needs a domestic source of armoured vehicles and the ability to replace equipment without waiting on foreign permission. This route concentrates state support on French tank production and the industrial capacity behind it. The approach improves supply security, but it commits capital to a heavy fleet and leaves France bearing the full cost of design, orders and maintenance.

European cooperation remains an alternate policy branch, with no foreign recipient or benefit.", 'source': 'French Ministry of Armed Forces archive (2021); Assemblee nationale PLF 2012 history of the arms delegation.', 'group': 'orthodox_gaullist'}

nodes.title: National Signals and Mobility
nodes.description: French command vehicles, radios and mobile support units link dispersed formations to national headquarters. Standardizing these systems improves field coordination and reduces logistical strain, while their electrical demands press on the military-industrial base. The policy reinforces independent operations without placing French units under an allied command, but requires long-term procurement and technical support at home.

nodes.title: Competitive Aircraft Contracts
nodes.description: Independent aircraft firms and export contracts can reward engineering quality, provided the state gives manufacturers room to compete. This programme backs performance-based contracts and a stable airframe series, accepting lower corporate receipts in exchange for stronger industrial incentives. French firms gain commercial freedom, while the government must tolerate uneven results and the risk that export priorities shape domestic production choices.

nodes.title: Export Certification and Avionics
nodes.description: Export certification and advanced avionics help French aircraft meet demanding foreign standards and keep design teams close to the latest systems. This route invests in technical education and air doctrine rather than expanding every production line. The return depends on sustained research and access to overseas markets; a downturn in orders would leave the state carrying the cost of specialized expertise.
nodes.history: {'basis': 'RI liberal and pro-European majority partner; Giscard reforms and economic adjustment.', 'source': 'history_evidence.md §16; Elysee Giscard chronology.', 'group': 'liberal'}

nodes.title: Repair Before Replacement
nodes.description: Replacing equipment less often can preserve public funds for training, maintenance and other national priorities. This route accepts a smaller arms-industrial footprint in exchange for lower equipment costs and longer service lives. It suits a government wary of permanent procurement growth, though a sudden crisis would expose the limits of an older inventory and the reduced capacity to surge new production.

nodes.title: Common Maintenance Fleets
nodes.description: Shared maintenance fleets let military and civilian operators rely on common utility vehicles and familiar repair procedures. Standard parts reduce supply burdens and keep equipment useful longer, while careful production planning prevents depots from becoming a substitute for all new investment. The policy favors sustainment over expansion and asks France to accept slower modernization in return for lower recurring costs.
nodes.history: {'basis': 'RI liberal and pro-European majority partner; Giscard reforms and economic adjustment.', 'source': 'history_evidence.md §16; Elysee Giscard chronology.', 'group': 'liberal'}

nodes.title: Regional Land-Supplier Compact
nodes.description: Regional suppliers can keep army vehicles available without requiring every part to come from a single national contractor. This compact spreads orders among French workshops and firms, supporting local employment and a responsive supply chain. Tax concessions make participation attractive, but smaller suppliers need common specifications and dependable contracts or the dispersed network will struggle to meet military demand.

nodes.title: Common Depot Standards
nodes.description: Common depot standards give units and regional workshops a shared language for inspecting, repairing and resupplying vehicles. Investment in training pays off in lower field consumption and more dependable service, though certification takes time and public support. The policy strengthens the army's reach through compatible local capacity rather than concentrating every repair decision in a central arsenal.

nodes.title: Escort and Shipyard Procurement
nodes.description: France's Atlantic and Mediterranean commitments depend on ships that can be built and maintained by its own dockyards. This route directs industrial effort toward escort vessels and naval infrastructure, accepting slower growth in land-armament output. It offers maritime presence and secure sea lines, but a shipyard programme ties up capital for years before new hulls can enter service.
nodes.history: {'basis': 'Centrist/Christian-democratic partners and plan-contract indicative planning.', 'source': 'history_evidence.md §§20,33; Assemblee nationale 1968-73 group records.', 'group': 'centre'}

nodes.title: Fleet Training and Refit
nodes.description: Fleet readiness rests on trained crews, regular exercises and refit schedules that keep ships available between deployments. This programme invests in naval doctrine and specialist education rather than simply increasing the number of hulls. Training improves coordination over time, but it is expensive and competes with immediate construction; the navy gains competence before it gains additional ships.
nodes.history: {'basis': 'Centrist/Christian-democratic partners and plan-contract indicative planning.', 'source': 'history_evidence.md §§20,33; Assemblee nationale 1968-73 group records.', 'group': 'centre'}

nodes.title: Open Engineering Trials
nodes.description: The Republic's engineering schools and test establishments can improve military equipment without making procurement an extension of any single manufacturer. Open trials invite competing designs and publish technical requirements to a wider field of French expertise. The result may be better suited to public needs, but research takes time and its benefits arrive before any clear increase in the production line.

nodes.title: Independent Test Establishments
nodes.description: Independent test establishments can make a new design easier to introduce without abandoning all the methods and tooling of its predecessor. Engineers compare components and production trials before ministers place a large order. nodes.description: Territorial units need affordable rifles and dependable equipment more than a prestige arsenal. This budget gives priority to basic infantry supply and lower purchase costs, while accepting a smaller production programme. nodes.title: Repair and Regional Tooling

The policy binds technical employment to social guarantees, raising the cost of the programme when production slows. spirits.title: Presidential Republic
spirits.desc: A strong presidency and a disciplined parliamentary majority give the government considerable initiative. Central direction also sustains an extensive administrative apparatus.
spirits.resolve: The shared institutional branch changes the settlement; party turnover does not remove the Republic.

spirits.title: Unsettled Social Compromise
spirits.desc: The upheaval of 1968 has left a contested settlement between organised labour, employers and the state. Wage concessions and electoral victory restored order, but confidence in the social bargain remains fragile.
spirits.resolve: Social Settlement replaces this once with Social Mistrust (Stability -2%, no efficiency-growth penalty). A compatible social or electoral reform can remove the original or residual spirit, as shown in each focus; the two removals never stack.

spirits.title: Uneven Modernisation
spirits.desc: Large industrial programmes have transformed France, while regional access and local development remain uneven. The state’s capacity for major industry is real, and so is the gap between the capital and the provinces.
spirits.resolve: Regional Authority or Prefectoral State replaces this once with Modern Industrial Base: its existing +5% civilian-industry construction bonus is retained, and its -5% infrastructure-construction penalty is removed. That +5% is not a new focus grant.

agreement_rules.dispatch: Completing a fixed-country focus gives that named recipient an ordinary country decision pair: Accept / Decline. France has no initial country-selection decision.
agreement_rules.setup_costs: Both sides must be able to pay the displayed PP and treasury costs at acceptance. Acceptance pays both and adds both spirits in one guarded transaction. Decline or expiry grants neither.
agreement_rules.government: The exact French party is required to propose and while pending. Accepted bilateral spirits survive government changes. Domestic party programme modifiers deactivate and return with their own government.
agreement_rules.duration: Indefinite; no annual renewal or yearly charge.
agreement_rules.validity: No war between signatories; no diplomatic, financial, economic or military Imperia sanctions in either direction. Withdrawal, lost sovereignty or a missing signatory ends both spirits.
agreement_rules.stacking: One active France-linked compact per family for each signatory, across all French parties. No duplicate family stacking. Several different families may coexist. Existing family agreement must be withdrawn before another offer is accepted.
agreement_rules.reissue: After a 180-day cooldown, the completed country focus permits a fixed-partner Reissue decision if no agreement/pending quote exists. No country picker; recipient gets fresh accept/decline decisions. No automatic reinstatement.
agreement_rules.maintenance: Only registered active counterpart entries, at most six France-linked families; bilateral sanction-array lookups. No daily every_country scans. Actual engine scope/lifecycle verification required at implementation.
agreement_rules.foreign_sovereignty: No forced access, alliance, war, ideology, equipment delivery, research completion or government change. Refusal never blocks domestic reform/research.
